chunks: Abu al-Husayn ibn Abi Jid al-Qummi informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Do not perform the obligatory prayer in the Ka'bah, for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not enter the Ka'bah during any hajj or 'umrah; rather, he entered it on the Day of the Conquest, the Conquest of Makkah, and he prayed two rak'ahs between the two pillars, and Usamah ibn Zayd was with him.

key_terms.الْعَمُودَيْنِ: the two pillars inside the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْمَكْتُوبَةَ: the obligatory salat prescribed by Allah

ai.seo_question: Can the obligatory prayer be performed inside the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling against performing the obligatory salat inside the Ka'bah. It supports the ruling by citing the practice of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, who did not enter the Ka'bah during hajj or 'umrah, though he did enter it at the time of the Conquest of Makkah and prayed two rak'ahs there.
